title: Power table construction
statement: Let a program be run under machine limits with memory size $S$, word bound $W$, and recursion depth bound, starting at depth $d$. Let $\mu$ be an initial memory, let $\mathrm{dst},L,b$ be natural numbers, and let $e,p$ be integers and $t$ a list of integers. If $S\le W$, the segment of length $L$ starting at $\mathrm{dst}$ fits in memory, and $(b^j)$ is at most $W$ for every $j\le L$, then the power-table procedure can execute within time $17L+8$ and leave a memory $\mu'$ whose segment at $\mathrm{dst}$ is $(1,b,b^2,\ldots,b^{L-1})$, with every location outside that segment unchanged.
hypotheses_covered: The machine limits $\mathrm{lim}$, program $P$, and depth $d$ are fixed
